title: Annual outcrop timing raises renewal-box age by 9-52 percent in six North Pacific runs at a fixed 10-year mean renewal time
abstract: We test whether intermittent winter outcrop acts like steady renewal with the same mean area. We use published annual North Pacific areas from 40 CMIP6 runs and an exact periodic, fixed-volume renewal box. At a fixed 10-year mean renewal time, six runs with zero mean-map area but some annual openings give mean ages of 10.89-15.24 years. Their median age increase is 14.3 percent; the median across all 30 runs with annual contact is 4.7 percent. At a 40-year mean renewal time, the six-run median increase is only 1.0 percent. We prove a sharp bound: for any nonnegative rate with repeating period T and mean rate 1/tau, mean age lies between tau and (T/2)coth[T/(2 tau)]. A single concentrated renewal pulse approaches the upper limit. Order shuffles show that the sequence adds age in several runs beyond the annual value distribution. These are conditional process calculations, not ocean age estimates. The area-to-volume law is not calibrated. The method preserves the distinction between zero mean-map area, intermittent surface contact and sustained renewal. Code, exact licensed aggregate inputs, source hashes and numerical checks are included.

display.caption: Exact periodic renewal ages from annual outcrop sequences. The mean renewal rate stays fixed. Red marks and the middle panel show six runs with zero area in their mean winter maps. Numerical renewal times are sensitivity choices, not measured ocean times.
